lockup.summary: The company, its directors, officers and current holders agree not to sell shares for 180 days after the offering becomes effective, unless the lead underwriter, Maxim, agrees in writing.

what: It sells NMN anti-aging dietary supplements in the U.S. and plans organ regeneration products from its parent company.
proceeds: The company expects to raise about $21.9 million after costs. It plans about 30% for skin regeneration sales and marketing, 20% for cartilage research and 20% for kidney research. The rest is for general business needs.
risks: Its results may swing widely because of many factors outside its control.
If it does not carry out its business priorities, its results and finances could suffer.
It keeps spending heavily on sales and marketing, and there is no promise that sales will rise much.
Product quality problems could hurt its brand and its business results.
It may face product liability claims and may not be able to get or keep enough insurance.
